name: Doctor's Cave Beach
label: Doctor's Cave Beach
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Jimmy Cliff Boulevard' (2 web pages); placed at the stretch of Jimmy Cliff Boulevard nearest the subject (our map tiles).
pin_note: Position from OpenStreetMap way/321284942: the middle of the OpenStreetMap outline 'Doctors Cave Beach' (520 m across).
notes: Montego Bay's most famous white-sand beach.

text.description:
From Jimmy Cliff Boulevard, the stretch of road known as the Hip Strip (formerly Gloucester Avenue), you can frame the beach bar and the busy frontage behind the sand. The shot has plenty of colour and gives a sense of everyday Jamaican street life, which a plain view of the water doesn't.

The beach has a long story. In 1880 Alexander James McCatty founded a sanatorium in Montego Bay and let his friends bathe at his small beach, which was entered through a cave. In 1906 he donated the property and a private members' club was formed, and that club still exists. In the 1920s an English osteopath, Herbert Barker, visited and wrote an article that helped make the beach famous. Today it is part of the protected Montego Bay Marine Park.

For your photos, use the street view for the colourful backdrop and the beach for the water. Inside the beach, a pier end is a good place to shoot the white sand and turquoise shallows with the shoreline curving away in front of you. The beach is privately run, so check the official site before you go. Keep your phone ready for people walking past, as they add life to the frame. If the street is busy, wait a moment for a gap rather than rushing the shot.
text.geographic_location: Doctor's Cave Beach is in Montego Bay's seafront tourist area, beside the Hip Strip (Jimmy Cliff Boulevard).
text.directions_text: There are no stations or tram stops nearby, so head for the Hip Strip area of Montego Bay (for example by taxi) and ask for Jimmy Cliff Boulevard. The middle of the beach is to the north-west, about 2 minutes on foot. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for the bar and street frontage as you see them. Switch to ultra-wide (0.5x) if you want to fit in more of the beach and the buildings behind. If your phone has a 2x-5x telephoto, use it to pick out details such as signs, painted walls and parasols.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand on Jimmy Cliff Boulevard (the stretch along the beach, known as the Hip Strip (formerly Gloucester Avenue)). The beach bar and the lively Hip Strip frontage behind the sand, giving a busier, colourful Jamaican street backdrop. The beach is to the north-west. From here you see the beach bar and the lively Hip Strip frontage behind the sand, which makes a busier, more colourful backdrop than the water alone.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and place the bar or the row of buildings on one of the lower lines, with the sand and some sky in the same frame. Keep the phone level so the buildings don't lean. For a different view, go through the beach gate to a pier end, where you can frame the white sand and turquoise shallows curving away in front of you.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the brightest part of the scene to focus, then slide the exposure down a little so the sky and white sand don't wash out. Try a Live Photo to catch people moving past.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Early morning is usually quieter, which gives you a cleaner street shot. Late afternoon can give warm light on the water if you also shoot from the beach.

text.access_note: The street is public, but the beach itself is privately run and may charge entry, so check the official site before you go.
claims_not_in_sources: The beach is privately run and entry is through a gate; the piers and sand are not freely accessible.
Days when cruise ships are in port can make the beach very crowded, and early mornings are usually quieter.
Professional shoots and drones may need permission from beach management.
Late-afternoon or golden-hour light can look warm on the water and bay.
A pier end on the beach gives a view of the white sand and turquoise shallows.

name: Gloucester Avenue (Hip Strip)
label: Hip Strip
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Gloucester Avenue' (2 web pages); placed at the stretch of Gloucester Avenue nearest the subject (our map tiles).
pin_note: Position from OSM N7080206523 (Hip Strip (Gloucester Ave)): kept: no OpenStreetMap object carries this Wikidata ID.
notes: The lively tourist strip along the coast with shops and restaurants.

text.description: Gloucester Avenue, known locally as the Hip Strip, is a main street of Montego Bay known for its street life. It is a long, busy road of colourful buildings, painted shopfronts and everyday street life, with glimpses of the sea along the way. That mix of colour and activity is what makes it so easy to photograph with a phone: there is always something happening in the foreground, and the road gives you natural lines to lead the eye. The strip is about 2 km long, so it is a stretch to stroll rather than a single spot. It is also sometimes labelled Jimmy Cliff Boulevard on maps. Rather than trying to capture it all in one picture, walk a short section and look for small scenes: a bright doorway, a hand-painted sign, a row of shopfronts with the sea at the far end. Include a person walking past for a sense of scale, but be polite and ask before photographing someone close up. Early morning or late afternoon is the best time, as there are fewer crowds and the street is easier to frame. Some visitors find parts of the street run down and report persistent touts, so keep your phone in hand rather than dangling, and be a little more careful in the evening. For a quieter alternative view of the colonial-era architecture and street life, try Sam Sharpe Square near the entrance to the strip.
text.geographic_location: Gloucester Avenue runs through the main tourist district of Montego Bay, with the sea visible along the road.
text.directions_text: No public transport stops are listed for this spot, so check a map for the best way to reach Gloucester Avenue (the Hip Strip) and walk from wherever you are dropped off. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for street scenes that look natural. Switch to ultra-wide (0.5x) for a whole row of colourful shopfronts, and use telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) to pick out signs, murals and details without stepping into people's way.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand on Gloucester Avenue. A stroll along the main street shows the colourful buildings, shopfronts and street life of the Hip Strip, with the sea visible along the road.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Switch on gridlines and use the road as a leading line, keeping the vertical lines of buildings straight. Put a colourful shopfront or a passer-by in the foreground and let the street recede behind. Keep the ultra-wide lens away from the edges of the frame, where faces and buildings can look stretched. For a different view, walk to Sam Sharpe Square near the entrance to the strip and frame the older architecture from there.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap to focus on a bright wall or sign, then slide the exposure down a little so the colours stay rich and the sky does not wash out. Try a Live Photo to catch moving people and traffic, and choose the best frame afterwards.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Early morning or late afternoon, when there are fewer crowds.

text.access_note: No closure is noted for Gloucester Avenue, but check locally before you go and take extra care in the evening.

name: St. James Parish Church
label: St. James Parish Churc
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Sam Sharpe Square' (2 web pages); placed at OpenStreetMap 'Sam Sharpe Square' (way/758142607): middle (22 m across).
pin_note: Position from OSM N7659681885 (Saint James Parish Church): kept: no OpenStreetMap object carries this Wikidata ID.
notes: Historic Anglican church in the town centre.

text.description:
St. James Parish Church is a place of worship in the middle of downtown Montego Bay, listed at Church Street, a short walk from Sam Sharpe Square. The two work well as a pair. The square gives you the wider downtown scene, and the churchyard gives you the closer picture.

From the square you can photograph the church as part of the historic streetscape. Think of it as an establishing shot of old Montego Bay with the church in its setting. I can't promise the church front is framed perfectly from the square, so treat it as a first stop and a fallback. If you can reach the churchyard, one recommended frame is the church's stone facade with the graveyard tombstones in the foreground. That gives the picture depth and a strong sense of age.

The outside of the church is reported to offer good photo opportunities, and many visitors also photograph the inside, where the mahogany pews and stained glass are the draw. Bear in mind that this is a working church, so be quiet and respectful, and don't photograph people at prayer. Services run early on Sundays, and opening times vary, so check before you go and don't plan a visit around a fixed time.

Keep your phone steady with both hands, tap the church to focus, and slide the exposure down a touch if the sky is bright, so the stonework doesn't wash out.
text.geographic_location: In downtown Montego Bay, on Church Street, a few minutes' walk from Sam Sharpe Square in the old town centre.
text.directions_text: Follow Church Street towards the church and take your closer photographs there. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for the street scene. Switch to the ultra-wide (0.5x) if you want more of the buildings around you. Use 2x or 3x telephoto, if your phone has it, for stonework and facade details.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand in Sam Sharpe Square. A broader downtown view that places the church within the historic streetscape, though I could not confirm from a source that the church facade is framed well from here. From here you get a broader downtown view that places the church within the historic streetscape. The church itself is to the south-east. Sam Sharpe Square nearby is another recommended viewpoint for the wider scene. For a closer, cleaner frame, walk on to the churchyard and photograph the facade over the tombstones.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: From where you stand or the square, include some of the street and surrounding old buildings so the church has context. Turn on gridlines and keep the verticals straight so the buildings don't lean. In the churchyard, crouch slightly and put a few tombstones low in the frame, with the stone facade behind them. If you can't get into the churchyard, the wider street view is the fallback.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the church to focus and lower the exposure slider a little if the sky is bright. Gridlines help keep the verticals straight. Inside, if photography is allowed, turn the flash off and use night mode on a steady surface for the stained glass and pews.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Morning or late afternoon usually gives softer light on the stonework, and it is also more comfortable for walking around. Avoid Sunday service times unless you are attending.

text.access_note: This is a working place of worship, and access to the churchyard and interior may be restricted, so check the church's Facebook page or local information for current hours before you go.
claims_not_in_sources: Morning or late afternoon usually gives softer light for photographing buildings.
Visitors should dress modestly and be quiet, and avoid photographing people at prayer, in a working church.
Leaning verticals can be reduced by keeping the phone level and using gridlines.
Tombstones low in the frame and a slightly crouched position add depth to the facade shot.
The walk of about 4 minutes is calculated from the 227 m distance.
